title: Sharp 22-wall minimum in the k<=6 lattice model
summary: Every strictly simple canonical45 disk with W<=21 and k<=6 illuminates every pair of distinct interior A marks, for every support. The known dark 22-wall example has k=4 and attains the bound inside this model. Thus this is a genuine sharp restricted minimum, not just a search finding.

title: Every orthogonal room with at most eight walls illuminates
summary: Every distinct real interior pair in every strictly simple orthogonal polygon with W<=8 illuminates, for arbitrary positive real dimensions. This includes L, U, unequal-floor T, offset-corridor and staircase shapes, all endpoint placements and limiting parameter equalities admitted by strict simplicity. There is no lattice, exception, area or aspect-ratio cap.

title: One-sided combs: no wall-count bound for spine/middle-row pairs
summary: In any rectangular-spine comb with arbitrarily many teeth on one side, every distinct pair drawn from the spine and the middle horizontal lines of teeth illuminates. Dimensions, tooth heights, widths and endpoint depths may be arbitrary real numbers. Extra unused teeth do not enter the construction.

title: Complete infinite two-sided comb subclasses through 21 walls
summary: These are actual all-pair A-mark theorems, without k, area, support or diameter caps:

title: Two arbitrary fixed chambers joined by a long neck
summary: Two fixed arbitrary-real orthogonal chambers joined through smooth mouths by a positive-width rectangular neck illuminate each fixed opposing-chamber pair for every sufficiently large real neck length. The threshold depends on the chamber/mouth/mark data and is locally uniform under nondegenerate perturbations. A separate constructive rational-data result extracts explicit beam intervals and thresholds.

title: Long-neck networks and exceptional arithmetic growth
summary: For fixed three-chamber/two-neck families, possible long-neck failures concentrate near finitely many rational length ratios, sharpened to finitely many weighted affine strips. Integer data leave finitely many offset arithmetic rays; those rays are not thereby illuminated.

title: Nested staircase sufficient conditions, beyond eight walls
summary: Accepted nested-band and bounding-triangle inequalities guarantee illumination for arbitrary real interior pairs in the stated multi-band staircase families. They keep one common slope through every portal and choose an actual target image. The geometric inequalities are essential; this is not an all-staircase theorem for arbitrary numbers of steps or dimensions. Priority unassessed.

title: Explicit reflection bounds at fixed three-star support
summary: At the fixed interior A support S=(0,0), U=(2,0), T=(2,2), the surplus-layer results include a 13-reflection bound for the stated second-surplus class, 37 for third surplus, and 32 for fourth surplus. The final fourth-surplus proof permits the classified remote attachments; it is not restricted to a fixed local drawing. Its W<=21 and k<=6 assumptions remain attached.

title: Sharp minimum within strict whole-copy parity folds
summary: For the exact construction class of whole congruent copies of a strict canonical base, with literal inverse-copy agreement and actual interior marks mapping to two distinct smooth boundary A points, a dark pair requires W>=22. The known example attains it. Diagonal bases and arbitrary initial rigid placements are included; the common-similarity extension has separate acceptance.

title: Positive ten-wall spiral progress
summary: TR04: all interior pairs in a specified nonoverlap ten-wall spiral under tall or wide thresholds. TR05: upper-cap-to-bottom pairs at every metric. Terminal-left/bottom pairs at complementary metrics remain open. TR06 refutes one iteration premise, pending independent review. November8: independently accepted all-native-pair coprime-period theorem for a restricted thin-cap spiral family; see dated follow-up for exact scope.

title: Exact per-room decision framework and reusable path certificates
summary: The labelled finite origami-orbit method gives an exact decision route for each valid fixed arithmetic room when its entire required finite orbit is exhausted. Capped undecided runs do not certify darkness. Exact rational trajectory guards certify paths for all tile completions satisfying their required/forbidden sets, not just one drawn room. These methods are central to reproducibility; unfolding/group actions/SAT proof certificates are established tools, not inventions claimed by this project.

title: A wall-bounded skeleton for every individual rational direction
summary: The first-return marked graph has exactly q(W+2)/2 edges, with q<=8, hence at most 92 for W<=21. It retains actual source/target sheets, absorbing corners, prongs and positive integer edge lengths. Its size is bounded while weights and the number of directions are not. It supplies no finite universal list of directions.

title: Finite geometric atlases and strip generators
summary: Every marked canonical45 W<=21 geometry lies in a finite family of rational-linear sign cells with unbounded integer deformation coefficients. The orthogonal subclass has a bounded-base description using at most 44 commuting even-gap insertions; a single gap exposes a tree of at most five parallel necks. These are exact structural reductions of infinite geometry, not finite optical verification or darkness-preserving compression. Priority of their elementary polyhedral ingredients is not claimed.

title: Globally available geometric simplification
summary: Horizontal/vertical section completion and isolated-corner completion preserve literal interior marks, strict simplicity and the lattice, and provide a strict decrease in reflex count down to a rectangle. That is a genuine global geometric result. The necessary optical implication from a simpler illuminated room to the original is unproved; unrestricted transfer is false at the known dark example.

title: Arithmetic bridges and genuine affine transfer
summary: The work classifies torus-covered four-direction rooms into similarity-rational or independently axis-rational classes and supplies exact endpoint/coordinate bridges under cited published results. This is a specialization/application of existing theory, not an asserted new general classification.

title: Local exact shooting, corner repair and interception lemmas
summary: Useful proved ingredients include: an exact arithmetic progression of target roots on a jointly guarded chamber interval; a sufficient width condition forcing a root; a one-floor-bounce repair under a supplied physical corridor; the regular-domain Farey triangle endpoint identity; and two kinds of supplied cone-chain configurations that force a second parity-distinct physical reflex corner under darkness.

title: Few walls do not bound primitive direction complexity
summary: An accepted square family already forces arbitrarily large primitive illuminating vectors, although its direct path has zero reflections. The work further rules out the proposed universal affine rank descent even in already illuminated squares. A bounded wall count cannot justify a direction cutoff or an axis terminal case.

title: No automatic geometric normalization or limiting argument
summary: Reviewed examples refute the proposed bounded similarity/global-affine normalization. Piecewise-affine rescaling cannot preserve all straight crossings unless interface derivatives agree. Illumination at rational or nearby inputs does not automatically pass to a limiting exact pair. Adding/removing mirrors can change illumination. These invalidate named proof routes, not the low-wall conjecture.

title: No unrestricted Euclidean whole-copy explanation of darkness
summary: The anisotropically stretched known dark Q100 remains dark under axial reflection-preserving scaling, but violates proved similarity-invariant bounds for the stated strict whole-copy factor class at its wall count. A separate repaired 43-wall beveled control defeats an unrestricted orthogonal-base-only converse while retaining a diagonal parity factor. Neither is a <=21-wall counterexample.

title: Separator, finite-blocker and abstract monodromy shortcuts are insufficient
summary: Darkness yields a genuine-cone separator and local excluded-chord inequalities in a marked geodesic triangulation. The accepted bounded triangulation counts do not force nine distinct reflex corners. Ordinary finite blocking is automatic for arithmetic torus covers and therefore supplies no special darkness obstruction. The reviewed Heisenberg example shows abstract monodromy transitivity is insufficient, but is not physically realizable as a room of this class; it is not a low-wall dark polygon.

title: A useful exact minimum of two reflections
summary: A verified fourteen-wall room has an actual pair with no direct path and no one-reflection path across any wall, but an exact legal two-reflection path. Thus the minimum for that pair is exactly two. It disproves universal one-wall repair, not illumination or a larger reflection bound. Related two- and four-reflex controls refute universal availability of the sufficient repair corridor and width criterion.

title: Three failed global joint-selection shortcuts
summary: A shortest complete-fiber path excludes the strict narrow cone angle needed by the triangle lemmas. On the fixed unit lattice, an exact all-word divisibility obstruction excludes the two short templates in dark Q100. Even after choosing two arms to one cone, physical symmetries cannot reduce their minimum sector angle below their original physical wedge separation. These leave arbitrary-weight, non-minimizing global existence open. Q0/Q100 have nine reflex corners and do not refute the eight-reflex goal.

title: The readable 22-wall dark construction
summary: The strictly simple orthogonal example made of three reflected five-square staircases has 22 walls, area 15 and a hand proof for two actual interior dark marks. Its seam/convex-corner handling and independent verification are valuable artifacts. Exact coordinate identity with that historical example is unresolved. The general 22-edge existence bound was already published. Present it as an explicit, verified construction or likely rediscovery, not confirmed original research.

title: Exact affine pair transport and uniform-source L criterion
summary: Conditional exact endpoint transport; explicit L target/shear hypotheses provide a uniform-source seed mechanism. Existing all-real L illumination already gives broader room coverage.

title: Scoped diagonal endpoint-moving construction
summary: Specified d=1 mod4 symmetric-L pairs admit an exact original-Ry-target seed. Not all pairs or all L rooms.

title: Affine compression counterexamples and full-group direction obstructions
summary: Exact-q coverage and any-given-lit-path compression fail at stated scopes. A surviving fixed one-left path requires norm shortening and cannot be sent to axes or diagonals by any genuine affine map; other directions remain open.

title: Limits of homological and local-geometric realization tests
summary: Absolute symplectic/period compatibility admits unrealizable shortening actions; an actual nonaffine same-surface deformation compresses a path. Neither refutes the whole-group minimum.
